# `sandloom.sdk.app`

The application composition root: `create_app` and the derived module list.

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, §5.7, Appendix C):

```python
app = create_app(default_modules=app_modules("helpdesk.modules"))
```

`from sandloom.sdk.app import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

## Advanced names

### `app_modules`

```python
def app_modules(package: str) -> list[str]
```

The dotted names of `package`'s module packages, sorted by name.

A subpackage counts when its `__init__.py` defines `register` (a
`define_module(...)` assignment or a `def register`); packages whose
name starts with `_` are skipped.

### `create_app`

```python
def create_app(
    *,
    default_modules: collections.abc.Sequence[str] = (),
    default_optional_modules: collections.abc.Sequence[str] = (),
    title: str = 'Sandloom Framework',
) -> fastapi.applications.FastAPI
```

Build a fully wired Sandloom application (kernel + modules + ops API).

`default_modules` apply only when the deployment configured no
`SANDLOOM_MODULES` (the platform root passes identity/tenancy/billing); with
the kernel defaults (empty) the module set comes from configuration
alone. Every module is required unless named in
`default_optional_modules` (defaulted lists only) or declared
`optional=True`.
